<x_0.0068><y_0.2094>The broad-leaved hornwrack, fig. to. when fresh taken out of the tea, is of a fpongy foft texture, and fmells very filthy; but when it has lain for fome time on the floors, it becomes ltiff and horny, like fome fort of withered leaves. Both furfaces, when examined by glaffles, appear to be covered with cells; and, when a piece of it is cut acrofs, one may difcover the thin membrane that ferves as a bafe to the cells of each surface. The form of the cells is very remarkable, each one being arched at the top, and contracted a little at the lower part of the fides to make way for the arches of the two next adjoining cells; fo that by this particular construction no room is loft. The entrance of the cells is immediately under the arch of each cell, and the walls of the cells feem to be fortified with spines. Juffieu difcovered fmall polyps extending themfelves out of thefe cells, which he has described in the memoirs of the Academy of Sciences 1742-- _f_, Gives the natural appearance of a leafy branch of this coralline. F i thows a crofs fection of a leaf, and difcovers the several partitions of the cells.<x_0.7314><y_0.5477><class_Text>

<x_0.0098><y_0.5469>At the entrance of many of the cells a fmall teflaceous body like a bivalve shell is difecovered : F 2, the figure of the cell, with the fhell in it; it is of a transfi-parent amber colour, fo clear that one may fee the dead animal through it, reprefented by the black foot.<x_0.7285><y_0.632><class_Text>

It is one of the consequences of tenure in chivalry: (See _Foodal System, KNIGHT-Service_, and TENURE). It is the determination of the tenure or difolution of the mutual bond between the lord and tenant, from the extinction of the blood of the latter by either natural or civil means : if he died without heirs of his blood, or if his blood was corrupted and stained by commiffion of treafon or felony; whereby every inheritable quality was entirely blotted out and abolished. In fuch cafes the land efcheated or fell back to the lord of the fee; that is, the tenure was determined by breach of the original condition, expreffed or implied in the feodal donation.
